text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Lebanon's trade deficit in the first ten months of 1996 is $5,315 million.
-The three-day parliament session to debate government's policy statement started on a hot note yesterday with attacks by opposition MPs against Prime Minister Hariri.
-Former prime Minister Hoss accused unnamed officials of becoming rich in an illegal way.
-Four private television stations banned from broadcasting news and political programmes declare that they will merge. Two private radio stations violated the ban.
-The weekly t-bill issue of November 21 raised 477.9 bln Lebanese pounds.
-Employees of the audiovisual media ventures ordered to close at the end of November demonstrated outside the parliament in protest.
-Syria supports the government's decision to ban demonstrations and the audiovisual media.
-One Israeli-allied South Lebanon Army militiaman was killed and others were wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon.
-The trial of a group of Lebanese men charged with collaborating with Israel continues.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora says the expected deficit of revenue against expenditure will be 45 percent at the end of 1996.
-The Paris-based International Chamber of Commerce has elected as its vice president the head of Beirut's commerce chamber Adnan Kassar.
-Dori Chamoun, head of the Christian rightwing National Liberal Party, says: "I did not meet (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu".
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir says: "Lebanon does not consist of feuding tribes that need a sponsor."
